rules.rule_name: Program Initialization Announcement
rules.rule_description: The program must announce its start before performing any processing, providing a clear audit trail marker in the output log.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Display 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference File Reader program (CBACT03C) is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' as the very first action before any file operations or record processing begins

rules.rule_name: Open Account Cross-Reference File for Sequential Reading
rules.rule_description: The Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) must be successfully opened in input mode before any record retrieval can begin. This is a mandatory prerequisite step for all subsequent record processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Open Account Cross-Reference File
Prepare file for sequential reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has displayed its start message and is ready to begin file processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file must be opened successfully in input mode, setting the processing status to successful (result = 0), so that sequential record reading can proceed

rules.rule_name: File Open Failure Terminates Program
rules.rule_description: If the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be opened, the program must immediately report the failure and halt all processing. No records can be processed without a successfully opened file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Error: Cannot Open File
Display Error & Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open operation does not complete successfully (file status is not '00'), setting the result to 12
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE', display the file status details, and immediately terminate abnormally — no record processing is attempted

rules.rule_name: Sequential Record Processing Loop Initiation
rules.rule_description: After the Account Cross-Reference file is successfully opened, the program enters a continuous sequential read loop to process every record in the file from beginning to end.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Iterative Record Processing
Begin sequential read loop

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) has been successfully opened for reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins iterative record processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must enter a sequential read loop that continues processing records as long as the end-of-file condition has not been signalled (END-OF-FILE flag is not 'Y'), ensuring every record in the file is processed

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Check Controls Loop Continuation
rules.rule_description: At the start of each loop iteration, the program checks whether the end of the Account Cross-Reference file has been reached. This check determines whether to continue reading records or to proceed to file closure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End of File
Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the sequential record processing loop
acceptance_criteria.When: The loop condition is evaluated at the beginning of each iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the end-of-file flag is 'Y' (all records processed), the loop must exit and proceed to close the file; if the end-of-file flag is 'N' (records remain), the program must proceed to read the next record

rules.rule_name: Read Next Cross-Reference Record Sequentially
rules.rule_description: When the end of file has not been reached, the program reads the next available record from the Account Cross-Reference file. Each record contains a 16-character Card Number and 34 characters of associated Cross-Reference data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Read Next Cross-Reference Record
Retrieve Card Number - 16 chars
and Cross-Reference Data - 34 chars

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the sequential read loop and the end-of-file flag is 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) into the CARD-XREF-RECORD structure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record containing the 16-character Card Number and 34-character Cross-Reference data is retrieved and made available for display; the read result is evaluated to determine the next action (success, end-of-file, or error)

rules.rule_name: Successful Record Read Triggers Display
rules.rule_description: When a Cross-Reference record is successfully retrieved from the file, it must be immediately displayed, and the processing loop must continue to retrieve the next record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Retrieved Successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read a record from the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The record is read successfully (file status is '00'), setting the result to 0 (AOK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the retrieved CARD-XREF-RECORD (containing Card Number and Cross-Reference data) and return to the loop to check for the next record

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detection Signals Loop Termination
rules.rule_description: When the last record in the Account Cross-Reference file has already been read and no more records are available, the program must signal that all records have been processed and stop the read loop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: End-of-File Detection
Signal program to stop reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read a record from the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation detects that there are no more records to read (file status is '10'), setting the result to 16 (EOF)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag must be set to 'Y', which will cause the processing loop to exit on its next condition check, and no further read attempts are made

rules.rule_name: Record Read Failure Terminates Program
rules.rule_description: If an unexpected error occurs while reading a record from the Account Cross-Reference file, the program must immediately report the failure and halt all processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Error: Cannot Read File
Display Error & Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read a record from the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation fails with an unexpected error (file status is neither '00' for success nor '10' for end-of-file), setting the result to 12
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE', display the file status details, and immediately terminate abnormally — no further records are processed

rules.rule_name: Display Retrieved Cross-Reference Record
rules.rule_description: Each successfully retrieved Cross-Reference record must be displayed to the output, showing the Card Number and its associated Account Cross-Reference data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Display Cross-Reference Record
Print Card Number and
Associated Account Cross-Reference Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read from the Account Cross-Reference file and the end-of-file flag remains 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the successfully retrieved record in the main processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete CARD-XREF-RECORD — containing the 16-character Card Number and 34-character Cross-Reference data — must be displayed to the output, after which the loop returns to check the end-of-file condition for the next iteration

rules.rule_name: Close Account Cross-Reference File After Processing
rules.rule_description: Once all records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been processed and the end-of-file condition is confirmed, the file must be properly closed before the program completes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Close Account Cross-Reference File
Close file after all records processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The sequential record processing loop has exited because the end-of-file flag is 'Y', indicating all records have been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file must be closed successfully (result set to 0), confirming that all file resources are properly released before program completion

rules.rule_name: File Close Failure Terminates Program
rules.rule_description: If the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be properly closed after all records are processed, the program must report the failure and halt abnormally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Error: Cannot Close File
Display Error & Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) after completing all record processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The file close operation does not complete successfully (file status is not '00'), setting the result to 12
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE', display the file status details, and immediately terminate abnormally

rules.rule_name: Program Completion Announcement
rules.rule_description: Upon successful completion of all record processing and file closure, the program must announce its successful end, providing a clear audit trail marker in the output log.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Program Completion
Display 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C'

acceptance_criteria.Given: All Cross-Reference records have been read and displayed, and the Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches its final step
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' as the last action before terminating normally

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing program CBACT03C is triggered for execution

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' to confirm that the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process has started

rules.rule_name: Open Account Cross-Reference File for Sequential Reading
rules.rule_description: The Account Cross-Reference file must be opened in read-only sequential mode before any record processing can begin. This is the mandatory first step to access card-to-account cross-reference data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Request to Open Account Cross-Reference File for Sequential Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) exists and contains card-to-account cross-reference records
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the process to open the Account Cross-Reference file for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Cross-Reference file is opened in input (read-only) mode, making it available for sequential record-by-record reading

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Opening of Account Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: After requesting to open the Account Cross-Reference file, the program must verify whether the file was made available successfully before proceeding with any record reading operations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Opened Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A request has been made to open the Account Cross-Reference file for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The file system returns the result of the open operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file was opened successfully, the file is marked as ready for sequential record reading and processing continues; if the file was not opened successfully, the program proceeds to error handling and termination

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Sequential Record Reading When File is Available
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully opened, the program confirms the file is ready and returns control to the main process to begin sequential reading of cross-reference records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Ready for Sequential Record Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully opened for input
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open operation is confirmed as successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file is marked as ready for sequential record reading and control is returned to the main process to begin reading card-to-account cross-reference records

rules.rule_name: Display Error Message When Account Cross-Reference File Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be opened, the program must notify the user with a descriptive error message identifying the file that failed to open, so the issue can be investigated and resolved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: Cannot Open Account Cross-Reference File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A request was made to open the Account Cross-Reference file for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open operation fails and the file is not available
acceptance_criteria.Then: An error message 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE' is displayed, and the file status details are displayed to identify the nature of the failure

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program When Account Cross-Reference File Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be opened, the program cannot continue processing and must terminate abnormally. This ensures no partial or incorrect processing occurs without access to the required cross-reference data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate Program with Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file failed to open and an error message has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The file unavailability is confirmed as an unrecoverable condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program is terminated abnormally, halting all further processing to prevent any incomplete or erroneous cross-reference data operations

rules.rule_name: Sequential Read of Next Cross-Reference Record
rules.rule_description: The system must sequentially retrieve the next available record from the Account Cross-Reference file into the cross-reference record buffer for processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Next Record from
Account Cross-Reference File
into CARD-XREF-RECORD

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully opened and is positioned at the next unread record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file using sequential access
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file and loads it into the cross-reference record buffer (CARD-XREF-RECORD) for further processing

rules.rule_name: Successful Cross-Reference Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a cross-reference record is successfully read, the system confirms retrieval and makes the record data available, consisting of a 16-character card number and 34 characters of associated cross-reference data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Retrieved:
Card Number - 16 Characters
Cross-Reference Data - 34 Characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes successfully and a record is found
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system confirms successful retrieval by setting the result indicator to success (0), and the cross-reference record buffer (CARD-XREF-RECORD) is populated with the card number (16 characters) and associated cross-reference data (34 characters), and the record is displayed

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detection on Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When no more records remain in the Account Cross-Reference file, the system must detect the end-of-file condition and signal the processing loop to stop reading.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Signal End of File:
Set END-OF-FILE = 'Y'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation returns an end-of-file condition indicating there are no more records to process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the result indicator to end-of-file (16), recognizes the end-of-file condition, sets the END-OF-FILE flag to 'Y', and returns control to the processing loop which will then terminate further record reads

rules.rule_name: Unexpected Error During Cross-Reference Record Read
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading from the Account Cross-Reference file (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file), the system must report the failure and immediately terminate processing to prevent data integrity issues.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Error: Failed to Read
Account Cross-Reference Record
Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation returns an unexpected error condition that is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the result indicator to error (12), displays the message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE', captures and displays the file status details, and terminates the program abnormally to prevent further processing

key_functionalities.title: Display Cross
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Display Cross-Reference Record])
    D1{Was Record\nRetrieved\nSuccessfully?}
    P1[Prepare Cross-Reference Record\nfor Display\nCard Number - 16 Characters\nAccount Cross-Reference Data - 34 Characters]
    P2[Display Complete\nCross-Reference Record\nCard Number + Account Cross-Reference Data]
    P3[Skip Display\nEnd of File or Error Condition]
    Z([Return to Record Processing Loop])

    A --> D1
    D1 -->|Yes - Record Retrieved Successfully| P1

rules.rule_name: Verify Record Retrieval Status Before Display
rules.rule_description: Before displaying a Cross-Reference record, the system must confirm that the record was retrieved successfully from the Cross-Reference file. Only records with a confirmed successful retrieval status proceed to display; end-of-file or error conditions are routed away from display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Record Retrieved Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The retrieval attempt completes and a retrieval status is available
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the retrieval was successful (record found and read without error), the record is marked as ready for display; if the retrieval resulted in end-of-file or an error condition, the record is not marked for display and the display step is bypassed

rules.rule_name: Display Cross-Reference Record Upon Successful Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a Cross-Reference record is successfully retrieved from the Cross-Reference file, the complete record — comprising the 16-character Card Number and the 34-character Account Cross-Reference Data — is immediately displayed as a single combined output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Complete Cross-Reference Record Card Number + Account Cross-Reference Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file with no errors and end-of-file has not been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the record retrieval was successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete Cross-Reference record is displayed, containing the Card Number (16 characters) concatenated with the Account Cross-Reference Data (34 characters), totalling 50 characters of cross-reference information

rules.rule_name: Prepare Cross-Reference Record Data for Display
rules.rule_description: Before displaying, the successfully retrieved Cross-Reference record is structured as a combined data unit consisting of a 16-character Card Number field and a 34-character Account Cross-Reference Data field, forming the complete record to be presented.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Cross-Reference Record for Display Card Number - 16 Characters Account Cross-Reference Data - 34 Characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: A record has been successfully read from the Card Cross-Reference file into the Cross-Reference record area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the record for output
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record is composed of exactly two data elements: the Card Number occupying 16 characters and the Account Cross-Reference Data occupying 34 characters, and the full 50-character record is made ready for display

rules.rule_name: Skip Record Display at End of File
rules.rule_description: When the Cross-Reference file has no more records to read (end-of-file condition), the display step is skipped entirely and the end-of-file indicator is set, causing the record processing loop to terminate without attempting to display any further records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip Display End of File or Error Condition

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Card Cross-Reference file and the end-of-file condition has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file status is detected after a read attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-file indicator is set to 'Yes', no record is displayed, and the record processing loop exits without performing any display action

rules.rule_name: Skip Record Display on Read Error and Halt Processing
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a record from the Cross-Reference file (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file), the display step is skipped, an error message is shown, and the program halts immediately to prevent processing of corrupt or incomplete data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip Display End of File or Error Condition

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Card Cross-Reference file and the result is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition
acceptance_criteria.When: An unexpected error condition is detected during the record read attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: No record is displayed, an error message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' is shown to indicate the Cross-Reference file read failure, and the program terminates immediately without processing any further records

rules.rule_name: Confirm End-of-File Not Reached Before Second Display in Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: Within the main record processing loop, after a read attempt, the system performs a secondary check to confirm that end-of-file has not been reached before displaying the record a second time, ensuring no spurious display occurs at the boundary of the file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Record Retrieved Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has just completed a read attempt within the main record processing loop and the read paragraph has already been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The main loop evaluates whether to display the record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the end-of-file indicator is still 'No' after the read attempt, the Cross-Reference record is displayed in the main loop; if the end-of-file indicator has been set to 'Yes' by the read attempt, the display in the main loop is skipped and the loop exits on the next iteration check

key_functionalities.title: End
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Read Record Attempt Complete])
    B{Was Last Record\nAlready Read?}
    C{Check File\nRead Status}
    D[Signal End of File:\nSet END-OF-FILE Flag to Yes]
    E([Return to Loop:\nStop Reading Records])
    F([Continue to\nDisplay Record])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - END-OF-FILE = Y| E
    B -->|No - END-OF-FILE = N| C
    C -->|File Status = 10\nNo More Records Available| D
    C -->|File Status = 00\nRecord Successfully Retrieved| F
    D --> E

rules.rule_name: Prevent Reading Beyond End of Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: Before attempting to read the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file, the program checks whether the end-of-file condition has already been signaled. If it has, no further read attempts are made and the program exits the processing loop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Last Record Already Read?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file processing loop is active and a previous read attempt has already signaled that all records have been exhausted (END-OF-FILE flag is set to Yes)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates whether to attempt reading the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must NOT attempt another read and must immediately exit the processing loop, stopping all further record retrieval from the Account Cross-Reference file

rules.rule_name: Detect Exhaustion of All Records in Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When a read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file returns a status indicating that no more records are available (end-of-file condition), the program must signal that all records have been processed so that the reading loop can be terminated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Status = 10 No More Records Available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file is open and being read sequentially, and the END-OF-FILE flag is currently set to No
acceptance_criteria.When: A read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file returns a file status indicating no more records are available (end-of-file reached)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must set the END-OF-FILE flag to Yes, signaling that all records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been processed, and must return control to the processing loop to trigger loop termination

rules.rule_name: Signal End-of-File to Stop Cross-Reference File Processing
rules.rule_description: Upon confirming that no more records exist in the Account Cross-Reference file, the program updates the END-OF-FILE indicator to Yes. This state change is the mechanism that communicates to the main processing loop that record retrieval is complete and iteration should cease.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Signal End of File: Set END-OF-FILE Flag to Yes

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file has confirmed that no further records are available
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the end-of-file condition returned from the Account Cross-Reference file read operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The END-OF-FILE flag must be set to Yes, and control must return to the main processing loop where the Yes value will cause the loop to terminate and no further records will be read

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful Record Retrieval and Continue to Display
rules.rule_description: When a record is successfully retrieved from the Account Cross-Reference file, the program confirms the successful read and proceeds to display the record. The END-OF-FILE flag remains set to No, allowing the processing loop to continue retrieving subsequent records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Status = 00 Record Successfully Retrieved

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file is open and being read sequentially, and the END-OF-FILE flag is currently set to No
acceptance_criteria.When: A read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file returns a status confirming that a record was successfully retrieved
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must confirm the read as successful, keep the END-OF-FILE flag set to No, and proceed to display the retrieved Cross-Reference record — allowing the processing loop to continue to the next iteration for subsequent records

rules.rule_name: Return to Processing Loop After End-of-File is Signaled
rules.rule_description: Once the END-OF-FILE flag has been set to Yes — either because it was already Yes before the read attempt or because the current read confirmed no more records exist — the program returns control to the main loop. The loop evaluates the Yes flag and terminates, stopping all further reads of the Account Cross-Reference file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to Loop: Stop Reading Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The END-OF-FILE flag has been set to Yes, either prior to the read attempt or as a result of the current read returning no more records
acceptance_criteria.When: Control is returned to the main processing loop for evaluation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The main processing loop must detect the END-OF-FILE flag as Yes and must exit the loop, ensuring no further read attempts are made against the Account Cross-Reference file

key_functionalities.title: Iterative Record Processing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Begin Iterative Record Processing])
    D1{Has End of File\nbeen Reached?}
    P1[Read Next Cross-Reference Record\nfrom Account Cross-Reference File]
    D2{Was Record\nRead Successfully?}
    P2[Display Cross-Reference Record\nCard Number and Associated\nAccount Cross-Reference Data]
    P3[Mark End of File\nSignal = Yes]
    E1[Display Read Error\nTerminate Program]
    Z([End of Iterative Processing\nAll Records Processed])

    A --> D1
    D1 -->|No - Continue Processing| P1
    P1 --> D2
    D2 -->|Record Retrieved Successfully| P2
    P2 --> D1
    D2 -->|End of File Detected| P3
    P3 --> D1
    D2 -->|Read Error Occurred| E1
    D1 -->|Yes - End of File Reached| Z

rules.rule_name: Continue Processing When End of File Not Yet Reached
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the iterative record processing loop should continue by checking if the end-of-file signal has been set. Processing continues only when the end-of-file has not yet been reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Has End of File been Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The iterative processing of the Account Cross-Reference File is active and the End-of-File Signal is currently set to 'No' (not yet reached)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File Signal at the start of each iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to read the next Cross-Reference Record from the Account Cross-Reference File

rules.rule_name: Terminate Loop When End of File Has Been Reached
rules.rule_description: Determines that iterative record processing must stop when the end-of-file signal has been set to 'Yes', signalling that all records in the Account Cross-Reference File have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Has End of File been Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The iterative processing of the Account Cross-Reference File is active and the End-of-File Signal is currently set to 'Yes'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File Signal at the start of an iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system exits the processing loop and moves to the End of Iterative Processing, indicating all Cross-Reference Records have been processed

rules.rule_name: Read Next Cross-Reference Record from Account Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: Retrieves the next sequential Cross-Reference Record from the Account Cross-Reference File into the Card Cross-Reference Record area for processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Cross-Reference Record from Account Cross-Reference File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference File is open for reading and the End-of-File Signal is 'No'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next record from the Account Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next Cross-Reference Record is retrieved and loaded into the Card Cross-Reference Record area, and the system evaluates whether the read was successful, end-of-file was detected, or a read error occurred

rules.rule_name: Display Cross-Reference Record on Successful Read
rules.rule_description: When a Cross-Reference Record is successfully retrieved from the Account Cross-Reference File, the full record containing the Card Number and its associated Account Cross-Reference data is displayed as output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Cross-Reference Record Card Number and Associated Account Cross-Reference Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation on the Account Cross-Reference File has been performed and the record was retrieved successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the record was read without error and the End-of-File Signal remains 'No'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the complete Cross-Reference Record, including the Card Number and all associated Account Cross-Reference data, and returns to check the End-of-File Signal for the next iteration

rules.rule_name: Mark End of File When Last Record Has Been Read
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference File signals that there are no more records to read, the End-of-File Signal is set to 'Yes' to indicate that all Cross-Reference Records have been processed and the loop should terminate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark End of File Signal = Yes

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation on the Account Cross-Reference File has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The file signals that the end of the file has been reached and there are no more Cross-Reference Records to retrieve
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the End-of-File Signal to 'Yes' and returns to the loop check, which will then terminate iterative processing

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program on Cross-Reference File Read Error
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading from the Account Cross-Reference File (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition), the system displays an error message and immediately terminates the program to prevent processing of incomplete or corrupt data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Read Error Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation on the Account Cross-Reference File has been performed and the result is neither a successful record retrieval nor an end-of-file signal
acceptance_criteria.When: An unexpected read error condition is detected on the Account Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' along with the file status details, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further Cross-Reference Records are processed

key_functionalities.title: Close Account Cross
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Close Account\nCross-Reference File])
    B[Attempt to Close\nAccount Cross-Reference File]
    XREFFILE[(XREFFILE\nVSAM KSDS\nAccount Cross-Reference)]
    C{File Closed\nSuccessfully?}
    D[File Closure\nConfirmed - No Errors]
    E[Display Error Message:\n'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE']
    F[Display Detailed\nFile Status Information]
    G[Terminate Program\nAbnormally]
    H([End: File Closed\nSuccessfully])

    A --> B
    B --> XREFFILE
    XREFFILE -.->|Close Operation| C
    C -->|Yes - Status OK| D
    C -->|No - Closure Failed| E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    D --> H

rules.rule_name: Close Account Cross-Reference File After Processing
rules.rule_description: The Account Cross-Reference file must be closed after all records have been fully processed. The close operation is only initiated once the end of the file has been reached and the read loop has completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Close Account Cross-Reference File

acceptance_criteria.Given: All records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been read and processed, and the end-of-file condition has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: A close operation is issued against the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE)

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful Closure of Account Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference file is closed without any errors, the closure is confirmed as successful and normal program completion proceeds.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Closure Confirmed - No Errors

acceptance_criteria.Given: A close operation has been issued against the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The file system confirms the file was closed successfully with no errors (file status equals success)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file closure is confirmed with no errors, the result is set to zero (no error condition), and the program proceeds to normal completion

rules.rule_name: Detect Failure to Close Account Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be closed properly, the failure must be detected and flagged so that appropriate error handling can be triggered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Closed Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A close operation has been issued against the Account Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The file system reports that the file was NOT closed successfully (file status is not a success code)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The closure failure is detected, an error result code (12) is set to indicate the failure condition, and error handling is triggered

rules.rule_name: Display Error Message When Account Cross-Reference File Cannot Be Closed
rules.rule_description: When the Account Cross-Reference file closure fails, a descriptive error message must be displayed to notify that the file could not be closed properly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file close operation has failed (error result code is set and the application is not in an all-OK state)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the result of the close operation and determines it was unsuccessful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' is displayed to the output

rules.rule_name: Display Detailed File Status Information on Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: Following the display of the closure error message, detailed file status information must be displayed to provide additional context about the nature of the closure failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Detailed File Status Information

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file close operation has failed and the error message 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the file status details for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file status is captured and detailed status information is displayed in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character status code, providing specific information about the closure failure

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program Abnormally on File Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: If the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be closed properly, the program must be terminated abnormally to prevent data integrity issues and signal the failure to the operations team.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate Program Abnormally

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file close operation has failed, the error message has been displayed, and detailed file status information has been shown
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine (CEE3ABD) with abend code 999, halting all further processing immediately

key_functionalities.title: Program Completion
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter: Program Completion])
    B[Display Message:\n'END OF EXECUTION OF\nPROGRAM CBACT03C']
    C([Program Successfully Completed\nControl Returned])

    A --> B
    B --> C

rules.rule_name: Program Completion Notification
rules.rule_description: Upon successful completion of all Account Cross-Reference file reading and display operations, the program must notify the user that the process has ended successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Message: 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has successfully completed reading and displaying all records from the Account Cross-Reference file, and the file has been closed without errors
acceptance_criteria.When: All records have been processed and the end-of-file condition has been reached
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' to confirm successful completion of the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process, and control is returned to the calling environment

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference File Reader program (CBACT03C) is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' as the very first action before any file operations or record processing begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must announce its start before performing any processing, providing a clear audit trail marker in the output log.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has displayed its start message and is ready to begin file processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file must be opened successfully in input mode, setting the processing status to successful (result = 0), so that sequential record reading can proceed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Account Cross-Reference File for Sequential Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) must be successfully opened in input mode before any record retrieval can begin. This is a mandatory prerequisite step for all subsequent record processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation does not complete successfully (file status is not '00'), setting the result to 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE', display the file status details, and immediately terminate abnormally — no record processing is attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: File Open Failure Terminates Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be opened, the program must immediately report the failure and halt all processing. No records can be processed without a successfully opened file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) has been successfully opened for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins iterative record processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must enter a sequential read loop that continues processing records as long as the end-of-file condition has not been signalled (END-OF-FILE flag is not 'Y'), ensuring every record in the file is processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Record Processing Loop Initiation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Account Cross-Reference file is successfully opened, the program enters a continuous sequential read loop to process every record in the file from beginning to end.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the sequential record processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The loop condition is evaluated at the beginning of each iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the end-of-file flag is 'Y' (all records processed), the loop must exit and proceed to close the file; if the end-of-file flag is 'N' (records remain), the program must proceed to read the next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Check Controls Loop Continuation
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of each loop iteration, the program checks whether the end of the Account Cross-Reference file has been reached. This check determines whether to continue reading records or to proceed to file closure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the sequential read loop and the end-of-file flag is 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) into the CARD-XREF-RECORD structure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record containing the 16-character Card Number and 34-character Cross-Reference data is retrieved and made available for display; the read result is evaluated to determine the next action (success, end-of-file, or error)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Cross-Reference Record Sequentially
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of file has not been reached, the program reads the next available record from the Account Cross-Reference file. Each record contains a 16-character Card Number and 34 characters of associated Cross-Reference data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read a record from the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is read successfully (file status is '00'), setting the result to 0 (AOK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the retrieved CARD-XREF-RECORD (containing Card Number and Cross-Reference data) and return to the loop to check for the next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Record Read Triggers Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Cross-Reference record is successfully retrieved from the file, it must be immediately displayed, and the processing loop must continue to retrieve the next record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read a record from the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation detects that there are no more records to read (file status is '10'), setting the result to 16 (EOF)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag must be set to 'Y', which will cause the processing loop to exit on its next condition check, and no further read attempts are made

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection Signals Loop Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the last record in the Account Cross-Reference file has already been read and no more records are available, the program must signal that all records have been processed and stop the read loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read a record from the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation fails with an unexpected error (file status is neither '00' for success nor '10' for end-of-file), setting the result to 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE', display the file status details, and immediately terminate abnormally — no further records are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Read Failure Terminates Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: If an unexpected error occurs while reading a record from the Account Cross-Reference file, the program must immediately report the failure and halt all processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read from the Account Cross-Reference file and the end-of-file flag remains 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the successfully retrieved record in the main processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete CARD-XREF-RECORD — containing the 16-character Card Number and 34-character Cross-Reference data — must be displayed to the output, after which the loop returns to check the end-of-file condition for the next iteration

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Retrieved Cross-Reference Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each successfully retrieved Cross-Reference record must be displayed to the output, showing the Card Number and its associated Account Cross-Reference data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The sequential record processing loop has exited because the end-of-file flag is 'Y', indicating all records have been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file must be closed successfully (result set to 0), confirming that all file resources are properly released before program completion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Account Cross-Reference File After Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been processed and the end-of-file condition is confirmed, the file must be properly closed before the program completes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) after completing all record processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file close operation does not complete successfully (file status is not '00'), setting the result to 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the error message 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE', display the file status details, and immediately terminate abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: File Close Failure Terminates Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be properly closed after all records are processed, the program must report the failure and halt abnormally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All Cross-Reference records have been read and displayed, and the Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches its final step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' as the last action before terminating normally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of all record processing and file closure, the program must announce its successful end, providing a clear audit trail marker in the output log.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing program CBACT03C is triggered for execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' to confirm that the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process has started

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Start Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process begins, the system must announce its start to confirm the process has been initiated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE) exists and contains card-to-account cross-reference records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the process to open the Account Cross-Reference file for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Cross-Reference file is opened in input (read-only) mode, making it available for sequential record-by-record reading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Account Cross-Reference File for Sequential Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Cross-Reference file must be opened in read-only sequential mode before any record processing can begin. This is the mandatory first step to access card-to-account cross-reference data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request has been made to open the Account Cross-Reference file for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file system returns the result of the open operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file was opened successfully, the file is marked as ready for sequential record reading and processing continues; if the file was not opened successfully, the program proceeds to error handling and termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Opening of Account Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting to open the Account Cross-Reference file, the program must verify whether the file was made available successfully before proceeding with any record reading operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully opened for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation is confirmed as successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file is marked as ready for sequential record reading and control is returned to the main process to begin reading card-to-account cross-reference records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Sequential Record Reading When File is Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully opened, the program confirms the file is ready and returns control to the main process to begin sequential reading of cross-reference records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request was made to open the Account Cross-Reference file for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation fails and the file is not available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An error message 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE' is displayed, and the file status details are displayed to identify the nature of the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Message When Account Cross-Reference File Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be opened, the program must notify the user with a descriptive error message identifying the file that failed to open, so the issue can be investigated and resolved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file failed to open and an error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file unavailability is confirmed as an unrecoverable condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is terminated abnormally, halting all further processing to prevent any incomplete or erroneous cross-reference data operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program When Account Cross-Reference File Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be opened, the program cannot continue processing and must terminate abnormally. This ensures no partial or incorrect processing occurs without access to the required cross-reference data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file has been successfully opened and is positioned at the next unread record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file using sequential access
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file and loads it into the cross-reference record buffer (CARD-XREF-RECORD) for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Read of Next Cross-Reference Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must sequentially retrieve the next available record from the Account Cross-Reference file into the cross-reference record buffer for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes successfully and a record is found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system confirms successful retrieval by setting the result indicator to success (0), and the cross-reference record buffer (CARD-XREF-RECORD) is populated with the card number (16 characters) and associated cross-reference data (34 characters), and the record is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Cross-Reference Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a cross-reference record is successfully read, the system confirms retrieval and makes the record data available, consisting of a 16-character card number and 34 characters of associated cross-reference data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns an end-of-file condition indicating there are no more records to process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the result indicator to end-of-file (16), recognizes the end-of-file condition, sets the END-OF-FILE flag to 'Y', and returns control to the processing loop which will then terminate further record reads

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection on Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no more records remain in the Account Cross-Reference file, the system must detect the end-of-file condition and signal the processing loop to stop reading.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns an unexpected error condition that is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the result indicator to error (12), displays the message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE', captures and displays the file status details, and terminates the program abnormally to prevent further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Error During Cross-Reference Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading from the Account Cross-Reference file (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file), the system must report the failure and immediately terminate processing to prevent data integrity issues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The retrieval attempt completes and a retrieval status is available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the retrieval was successful (record found and read without error), the record is marked as ready for display; if the retrieval resulted in end-of-file or an error condition, the record is not marked for display and the display step is bypassed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify Record Retrieval Status Before Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying a Cross-Reference record, the system must confirm that the record was retrieved successfully from the Cross-Reference file. Only records with a confirmed successful retrieval status proceed to display; end-of-file or error conditions are routed away from display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file with no errors and end-of-file has not been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the record retrieval was successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete Cross-Reference record is displayed, containing the Card Number (16 characters) concatenated with the Account Cross-Reference Data (34 characters), totalling 50 characters of cross-reference information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Cross-Reference Record Upon Successful Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Cross-Reference record is successfully retrieved from the Cross-Reference file, the complete record — comprising the 16-character Card Number and the 34-character Account Cross-Reference Data — is immediately displayed as a single combined output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A record has been successfully read from the Card Cross-Reference file into the Cross-Reference record area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the record for output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is composed of exactly two data elements: the Card Number occupying 16 characters and the Account Cross-Reference Data occupying 34 characters, and the full 50-character record is made ready for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Cross-Reference Record Data for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying, the successfully retrieved Cross-Reference record is structured as a combined data unit consisting of a 16-character Card Number field and a 34-character Account Cross-Reference Data field, forming the complete record to be presented.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Card Cross-Reference file and the end-of-file condition has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file status is detected after a read attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file indicator is set to 'Yes', no record is displayed, and the record processing loop exits without performing any display action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Record Display at End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Cross-Reference file has no more records to read (end-of-file condition), the display step is skipped entirely and the end-of-file indicator is set, causing the record processing loop to terminate without attempting to display any further records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Card Cross-Reference file and the result is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An unexpected error condition is detected during the record read attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No record is displayed, an error message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' is shown to indicate the Cross-Reference file read failure, and the program terminates immediately without processing any further records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Record Display on Read Error and Halt Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a record from the Cross-Reference file (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file), the display step is skipped, an error message is shown, and the program halts immediately to prevent processing of corrupt or incomplete data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has just completed a read attempt within the main record processing loop and the read paragraph has already been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main loop evaluates whether to display the record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the end-of-file indicator is still 'No' after the read attempt, the Cross-Reference record is displayed in the main loop; if the end-of-file indicator has been set to 'Yes' by the read attempt, the display in the main loop is skipped and the loop exits on the next iteration check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm End-of-File Not Reached Before Second Display in Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: Within the main record processing loop, after a read attempt, the system performs a secondary check to confirm that end-of-file has not been reached before displaying the record a second time, ensuring no spurious display occurs at the boundary of the file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file processing loop is active and a previous read attempt has already signaled that all records have been exhausted (END-OF-FILE flag is set to Yes)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates whether to attempt reading the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must NOT attempt another read and must immediately exit the processing loop, stopping all further record retrieval from the Account Cross-Reference file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prevent Reading Beyond End of Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to read the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file, the program checks whether the end-of-file condition has already been signaled. If it has, no further read attempts are made and the program exits the processing loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file is open and being read sequentially, and the END-OF-FILE flag is currently set to No
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file returns a file status indicating no more records are available (end-of-file reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must set the END-OF-FILE flag to Yes, signaling that all records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been processed, and must return control to the processing loop to trigger loop termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Exhaustion of All Records in Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file returns a status indicating that no more records are available (end-of-file condition), the program must signal that all records have been processed so that the reading loop can be terminated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file has confirmed that no further records are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the end-of-file condition returned from the Account Cross-Reference file read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The END-OF-FILE flag must be set to Yes, and control must return to the main processing loop where the Yes value will cause the loop to terminate and no further records will be read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Signal End-of-File to Stop Cross-Reference File Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon confirming that no more records exist in the Account Cross-Reference file, the program updates the END-OF-FILE indicator to Yes. This state change is the mechanism that communicates to the main processing loop that record retrieval is complete and iteration should cease.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file is open and being read sequentially, and the END-OF-FILE flag is currently set to No
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A read attempt on the Account Cross-Reference file returns a status confirming that a record was successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must confirm the read as successful, keep the END-OF-FILE flag set to No, and proceed to display the retrieved Cross-Reference record — allowing the processing loop to continue to the next iteration for subsequent records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Record Retrieval and Continue to Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a record is successfully retrieved from the Account Cross-Reference file, the program confirms the successful read and proceeds to display the record. The END-OF-FILE flag remains set to No, allowing the processing loop to continue retrieving subsequent records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The END-OF-FILE flag has been set to Yes, either prior to the read attempt or as a result of the current read returning no more records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Control is returned to the main processing loop for evaluation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The main processing loop must detect the END-OF-FILE flag as Yes and must exit the loop, ensuring no further read attempts are made against the Account Cross-Reference file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Processing Loop After End-of-File is Signaled
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the END-OF-FILE flag has been set to Yes — either because it was already Yes before the read attempt or because the current read confirmed no more records exist — the program returns control to the main loop. The loop evaluates the Yes flag and terminates, stopping all further reads of the Account Cross-Reference file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The iterative processing of the Account Cross-Reference File is active and the End-of-File Signal is currently set to 'No' (not yet reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File Signal at the start of each iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to read the next Cross-Reference Record from the Account Cross-Reference File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing When End of File Not Yet Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the iterative record processing loop should continue by checking if the end-of-file signal has been set. Processing continues only when the end-of-file has not yet been reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The iterative processing of the Account Cross-Reference File is active and the End-of-File Signal is currently set to 'Yes'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File Signal at the start of an iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system exits the processing loop and moves to the End of Iterative Processing, indicating all Cross-Reference Records have been processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Loop When End of File Has Been Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines that iterative record processing must stop when the end-of-file signal has been set to 'Yes', signalling that all records in the Account Cross-Reference File have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference File is open for reading and the End-of-File Signal is 'No'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next record from the Account Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next Cross-Reference Record is retrieved and loaded into the Card Cross-Reference Record area, and the system evaluates whether the read was successful, end-of-file was detected, or a read error occurred

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Cross-Reference Record from Account Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the next sequential Cross-Reference Record from the Account Cross-Reference File into the Card Cross-Reference Record area for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Account Cross-Reference File has been performed and the record was retrieved successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the record was read without error and the End-of-File Signal remains 'No'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the complete Cross-Reference Record, including the Card Number and all associated Account Cross-Reference data, and returns to check the End-of-File Signal for the next iteration

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Cross-Reference Record on Successful Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Cross-Reference Record is successfully retrieved from the Account Cross-Reference File, the full record containing the Card Number and its associated Account Cross-Reference data is displayed as output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Account Cross-Reference File has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file signals that the end of the file has been reached and there are no more Cross-Reference Records to retrieve
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the End-of-File Signal to 'Yes' and returns to the loop check, which will then terminate iterative processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark End of File When Last Record Has Been Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference File signals that there are no more records to read, the End-of-File Signal is set to 'Yes' to indicate that all Cross-Reference Records have been processed and the loop should terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Account Cross-Reference File has been performed and the result is neither a successful record retrieval nor an end-of-file signal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An unexpected read error condition is detected on the Account Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' along with the file status details, and immediately terminates the program abnormally — no further Cross-Reference Records are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program on Cross-Reference File Read Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading from the Account Cross-Reference File (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition), the system displays an error message and immediately terminates the program to prevent processing of incomplete or corrupt data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been read and processed, and the end-of-file condition has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A close operation is issued against the Account Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Account Cross-Reference File After Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Cross-Reference file must be closed after all records have been fully processed. The close operation is only initiated once the end of the file has been reached and the read loop has completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A close operation has been issued against the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file system confirms the file was closed successfully with no errors (file status equals success)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file closure is confirmed with no errors, the result is set to zero (no error condition), and the program proceeds to normal completion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Closure of Account Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file is closed without any errors, the closure is confirmed as successful and normal program completion proceeds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A close operation has been issued against the Account Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file system reports that the file was NOT closed successfully (file status is not a success code)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The closure failure is detected, an error result code (12) is set to indicate the failure condition, and error handling is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Failure to Close Account Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be closed properly, the failure must be detected and flagged so that appropriate error handling can be triggered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file close operation has failed (error result code is set and the application is not in an all-OK state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the result of the close operation and determines it was unsuccessful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' is displayed to the output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Message When Account Cross-Reference File Cannot Be Closed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Cross-Reference file closure fails, a descriptive error message must be displayed to notify that the file could not be closed properly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file close operation has failed and the error message 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the file status details for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file status is captured and detailed status information is displayed in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the four-character status code, providing specific information about the closure failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Detailed File Status Information on Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Following the display of the closure error message, detailed file status information must be displayed to provide additional context about the nature of the closure failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Cross-Reference file close operation has failed, the error message has been displayed, and detailed file status information has been shown
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is terminated abnormally by calling the system abend routine (CEE3ABD) with abend code 999, halting all further processing immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program Abnormally on File Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Account Cross-Reference file cannot be closed properly, the program must be terminated abnormally to prevent data integrity issues and signal the failure to the operations team.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully completed reading and displaying all records from the Account Cross-Reference file, and the file has been closed without errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All records have been processed and the end-of-file condition has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' to confirm successful completion of the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process, and control is returned to the calling environment

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of all Account Cross-Reference file reading and display operations, the program must notify the user that the process has ended successfully.

description:
CBACT03C is a batch COBOL program within the CardDemo application that reads and prints all records from an account cross-reference data file sequentially. It opens the indexed VSAM file, iterates through every record displaying each card cross-reference record to the output, and closes the file upon completion. This is a Main/Driver program with no external program calls other than an abend utility.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Display a message indicating the start of the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process 2: Open Account Cross-Reference File - Open the Account Cross-Reference data file to prepare it for sequential reading; terminate the program with an error if the file cannot be opened 3: Read Next Cross-Reference Record - Sequentially read the next record from the Account Cross-Reference file, retrieving the card number (16 characters) and associated cross-reference data (34 characters) 4: Display Cross-Reference Record - Print/display each successfully retrieved cross-reference record containing the card number and its associated account cross-reference data 5: End-of-File Detection - Detect when all records in the Account Cross-Reference file have been processed and signal the program to stop reading 6: Iterative Record Processing - Continuously read and display all cross-reference records sequentially until the end of the file is reached 7: Close Account Cross-Reference File - Close the Account Cross-Reference data file after all records have been processed; terminate the program with an error if the file cannot be closed properly 8: Program Completion - Display a message indicating the successful end of the Account Cross-Reference file reading and printing process
